query: What operational burdens appear in incident descriptions?

per_column.name: operational_burden_flags
per_column.rationale: This is a single multi-label field that packs all burden types into one pipe-delimited value rather than carving the concept into distinct, separately-named facet columns. The tokens (connectivity_issue, server_outage, access_denied, database_burden, email_service_burden, software_failure, performance_degradation, hardware_issue) are plausibly aspects OF operational burden, but they are collapsed into one column, so the column itself is a restatement of the whole concept, not a decomposition into MECE facets. It also mixes heterogeneous dimensions (fault type like server_outage/software_failure vs. affected service like email/database vs. symptom like performance_degradation), which are not mutually exclusive aspects.

per_column.name: operational_burden_count
per_column.rationale: A count of how many burden tokens were detected is a derived summary/cardinality metric of the concept, not a constitutive aspect OF the burden. It is a mechanical roll-up, not a facet.

per_column.name: primary_operational_burden
per_column.rationale: This selects the single dominant burden category, again re-labeling the whole concept rather than isolating one aspect of it. It is a classification of the concept, not a part-of facet.

judge.rationale: The technical claim requires the added columns to be constitutive facets (parts) of operational_burden, each an 'aspect OF' the concept realized as a separate, non-overlapping dimension. Instead, all three columns operate on a single flat taxonomy of burden categories: one packs every category into a multi-label field, one counts them, and one picks the primary one. None isolates a distinct constitutive aspect of the concept (e.g., a dedicated column per burden dimension such as service impact, resolution effort, recurrence, resource contention). The underlying category tokens are also not MECE among themselves: they conflate fault type, affected service, and symptom, so several can co-occur (connectivity_issue|server_outage|database_burden), violating mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is judged low because the schema captures only one axis (a type label) of the multi-dimensional notion of operational burden and omits effort, impact scope, and duration dimensions. The set is essentially a single multi-label classifier presented in three views, not a faceted decomposition, so it fails the test.
